messages:
Maria: Heads up — p99 jumped hard (~220ms -> ~1.1s) for a subset of hosted text-gen calls when the e2 fallback routing sent ~12% traffic cross-region to eu-west. Not steady-state but reproducible under bursty tails.
Tim: Which model/instance type? any kernel mismatches in the logs?
Maria: Mostly small-seq chat requests to rdl-13b-q4 on p4d. Profile + flamegraphs attached (link). Quick grep showed a lot of `copy_kv_to_host` and `wait_on_batch` stacks during the spike.
Sahil: KV cache misses? if routing changes cause cold KV lookups we can see tail blow up. Did you see a higher miss rate?
Maria: Yes — kv-hit dropped from 98% -> ~78% for the affected sessions right when fallback started. Latency correlates with first-token generation after a region boundary.
Jen: Could be that the fallback path picks a model variant with different kernel selection (int8 vs fp16) or different kernel set compiled. Kernel selection is chosen at load time — cross-region routing might pick a node that loaded a quantized runtime variant.
Oliver: I pulled the runtime logs for two example request IDs. The slower ones show microbatch size oscillation: batches of 1 interleaved with some 8s, so batching heuristics are failing to coalesce. We saw `microbatch_timeout_ms` set to 8 on those nodes (should be 4).
Tim: That would blow tail if small batches trigger more kernel launches and block on KV fetch. Can you share profiling numbers (kernel time vs memcpy vs sync)?
Maria: Quick summary from perf tool: kernel_exec 45ms -> 120ms (p99), memcpy H2D 8ms -> 42ms (p99), KV serialization/deser 4ms -> 22ms. Overall extra ~700ms at p99.
Sahil: So contributors: (1) cross-region cold KV => +20ms but amplified by (2) bad microbatching => +80-100ms per token due to kernel latency and poor batching, (3) maybe different kernel selection leading to slower matmul kernels under short-seq shapes.
Jen: Action items: 1) Force consistent kernel profile on fallback nodes (load same kernel set at start), 2) tighten microbatching timeout on fallback path to prefer slightly larger microbatches when throughput allows, 3) warm KV cache for session prefixes during routing change.
Oliver: I ran a small sim: forcing microbatch_timeout_ms=3 on eu-west nodes dropped p99 from 1.1s -> 420ms in the test harness (at same qps). When I also pre-warmed KV for the 30s window around the rollout, p99 went to ~260ms.
Tim: Nice. Do we have rollout knobs to apply this safely? Can we add a canary that toggles both kernel-set and microbatch timeout during a fallback?
Maria: We already have rollout flags. I'll create a short-lived route override that forces kernel-profile=v2 + microbatch_timeout_ms=3 for the fallback policy. Start with 2% of fallback traffic.
Sahil: Also log KV-hit by session_id and add alert if kv_hit < 90% during route changes. That will help catch regressions.
Jen: Please also record per-kernel latencies and sample flamegraphs at p95/p99 for each region so we can compare kernel selection differences.
perf-bot: perf-check — nightly profiling job scheduled for eu-west to run kernel comparator against us-east baseline at 02:30 UTC. Results will be posted in #eng-runtime.
Maria: I'll open a quick runbook for on-call: steps to force kernel set, how to revert microbatch timeout, and KV prewarm script. Plan: apply canary in the next 30m, monitor p95/p99 for 15m, then ramp.
Tim: Sounds good. If canary looks stable, we should bake the kernel-consistency into the fallback flow (so fallbacks always pick nodes with matching kernel sets).
Oliver: One more note: the batcher metrics we exposed (avg batch size, wait time, microbatch timeouts) need retention to 72h for debugging cross-region incidents. Filing a metrics retention ticket.
Maria: Thanks all — I'll post updates here after the canary. :rocket:
